content: Furthermore, these abandoned properties frequently devolve into illegal dumping grounds, exacerbating the long-term environmental damage and complicating equitable socio-economic transitions . The direct impacts of mining are also compounded by extensive indirect environmental damage. Regulatory compliance costs introduce another substantial layer of risk for property asset managers. The impact of these costs on asset management strategy involves heavy financial burdens associated with adhering to stringent mining laws and evolving government regulations. South African environmental and mining legislation is anchored in the "cradle to grave" principle, which was notably reaffirmed in a 2019 court ruling [62] . This principle mandates that mining companies and landholders bear full environmental responsibility for their operations from the initial commencement of activities through to post-closure and final rehabilitation . Asset managers also face significant administrative inefficiencies that complicate compliance and deter investment. For instance, the launch of a new mineral rights database, initially promised in 2024, has been riddled with bureaucratic setbacks, creating regulatory uncertainty and complicating land management processes [74] . These administrative barriers hinder effective remediation and contribute to the accumulation of liabilities, as peer-reviewed studies highlight ongoing shortcomings in the environmental management practices of mining entities [75] . The financial burden of maintaining compliance amidst such bureaucratic inertia requires asset managers to allocate disproportionate resources toward legal and administrative navigation, detracting from operational investments. While specific land risks are often viewed through an environmental or regulatory lens, the underlying economic viability of the property is inextricably linked to global market dynamics. This vulnerability forces asset managers to adopt highly adaptive financial models that can absorb periods of low profitability without compromising mandatory environmental and regulatory funding requirements. The inability to capitalize on emerging market booms due to systemic infrastructural and policy-related bottlenecks further diminishes the attractiveness of holding mining land as a long-term property asset.
